candidates.summary: plot_mover's second and third parts: inline get_mover_Y_x without its &C5 half (-19 cycles), drop the LDY mover that walk_column leaves in Y (-3), drop the CLC after the table ADC (-2), test the three-part types with CPX #5 instead of re-reading mover_types_parts (-2), JSR rows_up directly instead of subtract_Y_rows' STY/BEQ/JMP hop (-5). Byte-neutral: plot_mover_sprite &1AEA, leave_1f08 &1AFF and walk_column &1B0D do not move. Measured on the unshifted DEBUG_LIVES build, seed 1, pcprof 1500 passes: logic 9440 -> 9411 cycles a pass (-29); passlock 3000 passes seeds 1 and 3: state and screen identical. c2 and c3 are alternatives (overlap).
candidates.equivalence: (1) &C5 already holds movers_x_high,Y: plot_mover's first inline wrote it for this Y = mover, and get_mover_sprite_and_screen_addresses, the clip loops, move_to_next_column_in_XY, subtract_Y_rows/rows_up (ru_lo, ru_d are its own bytes), walk_column and plot_mover_sprite never write &C5 (grep of &C5 and its aliases result/source_address/zxbit: only multiply, scroll and mover-move code); the first part's inline already relies on this. So the old JSR get_mover_Y_x stored what was there; mover_x_low gets movers_x_low,Y as before; mover_y is not written by either. (2) Y = mover after JSR plot_mover_sprite: walk_column opens with LDY mover and no instruction after it (nor plot_mover_sprite's tail) writes Y; mover is written only by STY at plot_mover's entry. So the old LDY mover was redundant; Y indexes movers_x_low,Y (page aligned, as before) and later movers_frame_and_flip,Y. (3) C: ADC mover_types_second_sprite_offset,X ran with C = 0 (the BCS was not taken) and adds (frame AND 63) <= 63 to an offset <= &1E (the rows for types that get here), so the sum <= 93 and C = 0 after it; TAX, LDA, STA, LDA &7A do not touch C, so the CLC before ADC #&1C is redundant. (4) CPX #&05 / BCS: mover_types_parts is 0 exactly for types 0-4 and 1 or 2 for the other types below &1C (width, height and parts tables all have 28 entries); we get here only with parts < 2; old BNE left for parts <> 0, i.e. type >= 5; new BCS leaves for type >= 5; X = &7A as before for the third-sprite read. Exit flags differ (C = 1, Z from the CPX) but plot_mover's exits already differ in flags and every caller's next instruction after JSR plot_mover is an LDY/LDA/JSR/JMP/CLC/SEC that writes before reading. (5) JSR rows_up: subtract_Y_rows_from_screen_address_in_AX is STY unused_0076 / BEQ rts / JMP rows_up; the new code does the STY, then the JMP's target as a JSR, so rows_up's RTS returns to the next line as before; stack depth the same. With unused_0076 = 0 (the old BEQ path: only sprites_y_offset entries &00, types 9/10 at frame 0) rows_up leaves A and X alone (line >= 0, SBC 0 with C set, PLP, TAY, STZ, RTS), C and V as they came; it also writes ru_lo (written before read in rows_up) and Y = A where the old path left Y = 0; Y is reloaded by walk_column before any use, and unused_0076 ends 0 as before.
candidates.relies_on: Page crossings: none moved. The window is byte-neutral (+2 inline get_mover_Y_x, -2 LDY mover, -1 CLC, -1 CPX/BCS for LDA/BNE, +2 STY/JSR rows_up = 0), checked in the listing of the unshifted DEBUG_LIVES build: plot_mover_sprite &1AEA, leave_1f08 &1AFF, walk_column &1B0D identical. The in-window BCS leave_1f08 stays page 1A to page 1A. JSR rows_up targets &0A34 (moved_0a20, copied down before play; the old JMP already ran there). Relies on: walk_column leaving Y = mover; mover_types_parts being 0 only for types 0-4 and every mover type being below &1C (the type tables are 28 entries); the 63 + &1E < 256 bound on the sprite index; &C5 untouched by the second part's calls.

candidates.summary: Alternative to the first (overlaps it): the same plus dropping the CLC before ADC #&08 for the third part (C = 0 from the CPX #5 that fell through): 1 byte shorter and 2 cycles on the three-part movers (~0.7 a pass). It slides plot_mover_sprite, leave_1f08, walk_column and all after down one byte (walk_column &1B0D -> &1B0C). Measured, same profile: logic 9440 -> 9410 (first: 9411). Only the gate can say whether the slide costs a page crossing elsewhere.
candidates.equivalence: As the first candidate, plus: BCS leave_1f08 not taken means X < 5 so C = 0 (CPX sets C for X >= 5); LDA y_offset does not touch C; so ADC #&08 without the CLC adds exactly 8 as before. C after the ADC is 0 in both versions (y_offset <= &17, + 8 cannot carry) and nothing reads C between there and get_sprite_and_screen_addresses_for_frame_A, which does not read it on entry.
candidates.relies_on: Everything the first relies on, plus a one-byte slide of plot_mover_sprite (&1AEA -> &1AE9), leave_1f08 (&1AFF -> &1AFE), walk_column (&1B0D -> &1B0C) and the code after them. walk_column stays inside page &1B (&1B0C-&1B62) and the other indexed reads in the moved range were not enumerated; the SKIP 13 after leave_1f08 is outside the window and cannot absorb it.
